extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and litigators handling PTAB inter partes reviews (IPRs)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and strategy for whether the USPTO Director / PTAB will exercise discretion to institute an IPR. Covers statutory standard, Fintiv factors, stipulation types, Stewart memo process, briefing limits, and practical guideposts from recent PTAB decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. § 314(a) reasonable likelihood standard
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Director may not authorize an inter partes review to be instituted unless the Director determines that the information presented in the petition ... and any response ... shows that there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least 1 of the claims challenged in the petition.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory threshold for institution based on merits; quoted verbatim from § 314(a). This remains the merits standard separate from the Director's discretion whether to institute on discretionary grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's discretion to institute (not compelled)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Director is permitted, but never compelled, to institute an IPR[, a]nd no petitioner has a right to such institution.” (Mylan Labs. v. Janssen, 989 F.3d 1375, 1382 (Fed. Cir. 2021))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces that institution is discretionary even if statutory elements are satisfied; institution decisions can be denied on discretionary grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor — Stay in parallel litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the court has granted a stay or there is evidence that a stay may be granted if a proceeding is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the core Fintiv factors considered when deciding discretionary denial based on co-pending litigation (Apple Inc. v. Fintiv, Inc.). A granted or likely stay favors discretionary denial of IPR institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor — Trial date proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: The proximity of the court’s trial date to the PTAB’s projected statutory deadline for a final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often the primary Fintiv consideration; a near trial date (relative to PTAB FWD) weighs in favor of discretionary denial. Slides and cases reflect that trial date frequently drives denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor — Investment in parallel proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment: the investment in the parallel proceeding by the court and the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of resources already expended in parallel litigation. Greater investment tends to favor discretionary denial to avoid duplicative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor — Overlap of issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlap: the overlap between issues raised in the petition and in the parallel proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High overlap between IPR petition grounds and issues in district-court litigation favors discretionary denial to prevent conflicting outcomes and duplicative efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor — Identity of parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties: whether the petitioner and the defendant in the parallel proceeding are the same party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the same parties are involved in parallel litigation, that weighs toward discretionary denial because of duplicative adjudication risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor — Other circumstances (including merits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other circumstances that impact the PTAB’s exercise of discretion, including the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catch-all factor; tribunals consider additional context (e.g., meritoriousness of the petition, unique equities) when balancing whether to deny institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sotera stipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipulation not to pursue same grounds or any grounds that could have reasonably been raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A procedural commitment by petitioner to limit parallel challenges; historically has been used to reduce overlap concerns and influence discretionary-denial analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sotera Plus stipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sotera stipulation that also stipulates not to pursue, e.g.: petition art with unpublished system art; any system art embodied by prior art that could have been raised in IPR; any 102/103 arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broader-than-Sotera stipulation intended to further reduce overlap; may be considered favorably but does not guarantee avoiding discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sand stipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipulation not to pursue same grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A narrower stipulation focused on identical grounds; can be relevant but may have limited weight depending on trial date and other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sand Plus stipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipulation not to pursue any ground that includes the references asserted at PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broader Sand-style stipulation intended to eliminate overlap with PTAB-asserted references; may help but is not dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: June 2022 Director memo (prior guidance) exceptions to discretionary denial
rubrics_metrics.description: June 2022 memo instructed PTAB would not discretionarily deny institution where: petition presented compelling merits; parallel litigation was in the ITC; petitioner offered Sotera stipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical guidance now rescinded (2/28/2025), but important for understanding prior Office practice and where petitioners previously relied to avoid discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bifurcated institution procedure (Stewart Memo)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution decisions bifurcated between: (1) discretionary considerations (Director); and (2) merits and other non-discretionary statutory considerations (APJ merits panel). Director will decide whether discretionary denial is appropriate; if not, Director refers proceeding to merits panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process change creates separate briefing and decision points: a discretionary briefing to the Director and separate merits consideration by an APJ panel if referred. A discretionary denial ends the proceeding and is not appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary briefing page/word limits and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Discretion briefing page limits — Request due on/after 9/1/2025: 20 pages for request/opposition; Request due before 9/1/2025: 14,000 words for request/opposition. Discretion opposition deadline: same date as patent owner preliminary response (3 months after notice of filing date accorded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict page/word limits and synchronized deadlines require concise discretionary briefing; Office may update webpage periodically without notice. Plan filings to comply with page/word constraints and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Stewart Memo discretion factor — prior adjudication by PTAB/other forum
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the PTAB or another forum has already adjudicated the validity or patentability of the challenged patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If validity has already been adjudicated in another forum, that weighs in favor of discretionary denial to avoid duplicative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Stewart Memo discretion factor — changes in law or new precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there have been changes in the law or new judicial precedent issued since issuance of the claims that may affect patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New controlling law or precedent that materially impacts the patentability analysis may weigh against discretionary denial (i.e., favor institution) if it changes the merits landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Stewart Memo discretion factor — strength of the unpatentability challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: The strength of the unpatentability challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compelling merits showing can counsel against discretionary denial even when other factors point toward denial; petitioners should emphasize persuasive evidence and arguments on merits in discretionary briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Stewart Memo discretion factor — extent of petition’s reliance on expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of the petition’s reliance on expert testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heavy reliance on expert testimony (as opposed to documentary/prior-art-based arguments) may be weighed as part of the Director's discretion analysis; quantify and justify expert reliance in discretionary briefings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settled expectations (as a discretion factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Settled expectations of the parties, such as the length of time the claims have been in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every discretionary brief should address 'settled expectations.' No bright-line rule, but generally the longer a patent has been in force the more settled expectations weigh toward denial. Acting Director examples suggest outcomes where patents ~6+ years in force often have strong settled expectations, but PO may show strong expectations for younger patents with concrete facts. Petitioners must anticipate and rebut settled-expectations arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling economic, public health, or national security interests (narrowly tailored)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compelling economic, public health, or national security interests are a factor in discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments asserting these interests must be 'narrowly tailored'—i.e., explain with specificity why review of the particular patent(s) is necessary for those interests. Broad or generalized assertions are insufficient (see TSMC v. Marlin Semiconductor example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Catch-all: any other considerations bearing on Director's discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other considerations bearing on the Director's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may consider other equities or policy concerns not enumerated; parties should present any unique or extraordinary circumstances that might tilt the discretionary balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and procedural sequencing for bifurcated process
rubrics_metrics.description: Schematic timeline: PO brief (20 pages), petitioner opposition (20 pages), PO reply (if authorized), Director decision (with specified month intervals), and if no discretionary denial, PO preliminary response (14,000 words) and APJ merits panel steps culminating in a three-APJ institution decision (statutory maximum schedule indicated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand and follow the sequential deadlines and the fact that a discretionary denial ends the proceeding (not appealable). The slides specify months allocated to each stage (e.g., 2 months, 1 month intervals) and that institution decision by APJs must be within statutory maximum from PO preliminary response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on petitioner to show why petition should be instituted
rubrics_metrics.description: It is Petitioner’s responsibility 'not only to respond to patent owner’s arguments but also to identify reasons not to exercise discretion to deny institution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must proactively brief why discretionary denial would be inappropriate, addressing Fintiv factors, settled expectations, stipulations, public-interest claims, and strength of the merits. Failure to address these issues can lead to discretionary denial (see Dabico Airport Solutions v. AXA Power).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictors of referred (proceed to merits) vs denied petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Patterns: Referred petitions often have Fintiv factors weighing against discretionary denial (or close), patents <6 years old, and lack of arguments favoring denial; Denied petitions often have Fintiv factors (primarily trial date) weighing for denial, patents >6 years old, or absent persuasive counterarguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical patterns (as reported) to assess institution risk: trial date and patent age are recurrent drivers. Petitioners should tailor strategy if factors align with typical denial patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and weight of stipulations in discretion analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Acting Director may fault a petitioner for not providing a stipulation, but she will not necessarily credit a petitioner for providing a stipulation. A stipulation of any scope may not outweigh a trial date before FWD. However, failing to provide a stipulation may be weighed in favor of discretionary denial even if FWD will come before trial date (or there is no trial date or case is stayed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulations can help reduce overlap concerns but are not dispositive. Office decisions show that absence of any stipulation can be a negative factor; conversely, a stipulation does not guarantee institution where other factors (e.g., imminent trial) strongly favor denial.
